title: A verdict token that is absent must not default to the destructive answer
statement: When a machine-parsed verdict decides ship-versus-revert, never let a missing token default to the destructive outcome; write the verdict early on decisive evidence and budget verification so a timeout cannot erase it.
rationale: A verification stage under a hard cap can die before emitting its token. If absence is read as revert, correct all-green work is destroyed by a clock, not a judgment.
applies_when: A gate parses a token to decide accept/reject
The gate runs under a time limit
not_when: No automated verdict is parsed (a human decides)
how: Decide on decisive evidence only (suite result plus tree state) and write the token by a wall-clock deadline
Make the safe outcome the default when the token is absent, or fail into a hold state, not a destroy state
Keep lower-priority audits as follow-ups, not preconditions for the verdict
check: If the verdict stage is killed before writing anything, what happens? If the answer is 'the work is reverted', the default is unsafe.
failure_if_absent: Green, shippable work is silently reverted because the gate ran out of time before saying 'ship'.

evidence.title: agent-failure-modes INC-0005 - a killed step with no verdict token is read as reverted
evidence.quote: A machine-parsed verdict token that defaults to the destructive answer on absence is a critical safety hazard when its writer runs under a hard timeout
